neighbours.label: 'and'/'or' joining two predicates or nouns that share the complement after them, usually a to-infinitive ('willing and able to', 'the right and the duty to', 'permits or even encourages')
fire: We are looking for people who are ready and able to help at the food bank.
The program allows or even requires schools to test students twice a year.
Every parent has the right and the obligation to send their child to school.
She was happy (and proud!) to lead the parade through town.
The club needs members who are willing and eager to organize events.
Managers have the power and the duty to protect workers from harm.
The rules permit or encourage players to trade cards after each round.
I am still able (and glad) to swim a mile every morning.
quiet: We bought bread and cheese at the food bank sale.
The program tests students in math and reading twice a year.
Every parent packed sandwiches and apples for the school trip.
She smiled and waved as she led the parade through town.
The club meets on Mondays and Thursdays in the library.
Managers and workers ate lunch together in the cafeteria.
Players can trade cards or coins after each round.
I swim a mile and then eat breakfast every morning.
